From: Sam Patel <sam@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Intro + quick discovery

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciate the clear rundown. Quick notes from our side so we have alignment: 

- Pain: our current embeddings/search pipeline plus the chat UX is suffering from long tail latency. We see p95 generation latency around 1.2s for short queries but spikes past 2.5s during higher concurrency. Streaming feels choppy — tokens arrive in bursts and the UI stutters.
- Current stack: self-hosted Llama 2 34B (quantized) on GCP A2 VMs behind a custom API gateway; some requests routed via an internal cache layer.
- Concurrency: baseline 150 qps, intermittent spikes to ~600 qps (during batch ingestion and morning peaks).
- Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn short prompts, streaming token latency < 50ms between delivered token chunks, sustained throughput for 500 qps with graceful degradation and no 5xx during spikes.

Next steps from Finly: share a recent load test and traces (we'll attach the short report). We're also interested in a 2-week PoC to validate p95 and streaming UX.

Thanks,
Sam
Senior Product Manager, Finly

Sam, thanks — this is super helpful and aligns with what we heard. Recap from our side with specific items so we have a mutual action plan: 

1) Key pain points you confirmed
   - p95 generation latency frequently > 1s, spikes to 2.5s under load
   - Streaming UX is inconsistent: client receives token bursts, not a steady stream
   - Cache misses and backend cold starts amplify tail latency

2) Success criteria (mapped to Redwood deliverables)
   - p95 token generation for short prompts <= 250ms (target) / <= 350ms (acceptable)
   - Streaming token inter-arrival < 50ms for interactive sessions
   - Support sustained 500 qps with auto-fallback to lower-cost variants without user-visible errors

3) What we need from Finly to size a PoC
   - Recent load test (qps distribution, request sizes) — you mentioned you'll attach
   - Example prompt shapes and average token lengths for interactive flows
   - Allowed maintenance windows for traffic mirroring during PoC

4) Redwood PoC proposal (high level)
   - 2-week PoC: mirror a slice of traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool (isolated) + streaming client integration tests
   - Deliverables: p95 latency report, streaming token timing profile, suggested batching/quantization config, and recommended autoscale settings

5) Timeline & next steps
   - We can provision a Dedicated trial pool within 5 business days after we get the load test and token profiles
   - Proposed follow-up: technical kickoff w/ Aditya + Finly infra (30–45m) — proposed slots Tue/Wed next week

Attaching a short summary doc and a sketch of how we would route streaming requests and handle KV cache warmups.

I'll wait for the load test and then Aditya will propose a PoC config.

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Date: 2027-04-25T17:05:00-07:00
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Subject: RE: Discovery recap: latency & concurrency goals (p95 targets, streaming UX) - Finly

Adding a few technical clarifications from our side: 

- When you say p95 1.2s, do you have distribution by prompt length? Small prompts (<=64 tokens output) are usually dominated by kernel launch and attention setup — we can optimize with pinned model instances + fast KV cache warmup.
- For streaming UX: we typically recommend a combination of small token chunk sizes (e.g., 8–16 tokens) + client-side jitter smoothing (20–50ms) to avoid burst perception. We can instrument the streaming pipeline to report token inter-arrival histograms for the PoC.
- Concurrency sizing: to sustain ~500 qps of short-turn chat at p95 250ms, we'll likely recommend a mix of batching (to reduce per-token cost) and pinned low-latency replicas for hot prefixes. We'll propose a config with dedicated low-latency pool + autoscale buffer for spikes.

I'll draft a preliminary PoC config after I review your load test. Also curious if Finly is open to testing a quantized 16-bit inference path vs current 8-bit quantized – there's a tradeoff between latency and quality we can measure.

-Aditya
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
